properties.name: 1883 Krakatau Volcanic Eruption & Tsunami
properties.description: Cataclysmic volcanic eruption of Krakatau culminating in caldera collapse, atmospheric shockwaves, global temperature reduction, and destructive tsunamis.
properties.evidence_description: Documented 1883 eruption logs, tide gauge sea-level records, barometric shockwave traces, and coastal tsunami inundation surveys.
properties.evidence_significance: Tide gauge and barometric instrument logs provide historical record evidence supporting catastrophic caldera collapse and tsunami generation.
properties.geological_explanation: Paroxysmal eruption and collapse of the Krakatau volcanic island structure displaced huge ocean water masses, creating tsunamis over 30 meters high along Sunda Strait coastal shores.
properties.why_it_matters: The 1883 Krakatau eruption was one of the first globally recorded natural disasters. It demonstrated how volcanic caldera collapse can trigger ocean-wide tsunamis and global atmospheric cooling.
properties.source: Self (1884) / NOAA NCEI Historical Tsunami Database
properties.geometry_note: Point-based representation of Krakatau island epicenter

properties.name: 2004 Indian Ocean Earthquake & Tsunami
properties.description: A massive Mw 9.1 megathrust earthquake off northern Sumatra that generated catastrophic ocean-wide tsunamis affecting coastal Indian Ocean communities.
properties.evidence_description: Global seismic network broadband seismograms, satellite altimetry seafloor displacement measurements, and coastal tsunami inundation field logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Instrumental seismograms and GPS displacement measurements provide quantitative evidence supporting massive megathrust subduction fault rupture.
properties.geological_explanation: A 1,300 km long seafloor fault rupture along the Sunda Megathrust subduction zone rapidly uplifted ocean floor sediment by several meters, transferring immense energy into ocean waves.
properties.why_it_matters: The 2004 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake reshaped modern seismology and tsunami science, demonstrating the devastating energy release of subduction megathrust ruptures and driving the creation of global tsunami warning networks.
properties.source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (Event ID official20041226005853450_30)

properties.name: 2006 Yogyakarta Earthquake
properties.description: A shallow Mw 6.3 intraplate strike-slip earthquake centered south of Yogyakarta near the Opak Fault zone, causing major structural damage in Bantul.
properties.evidence_description: Strong-motion accelerograph records, shallow Opak fault lineament mapping, and structural damage surveys across Bantul sediment basins.
properties.evidence_significance: Instrumental ground motion records and fault mapping provide evidence consistent with shallow intraplate strike-slip faulting in sediment basins.
properties.geological_explanation: Tectonic stress release along a shallow strike-slip fault system produced severe high-frequency ground motion across soft volcanic sediment and alluvial soils of the Opak River basin.
properties.why_it_matters: The 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake highlighted the vulnerability of volcanic sediment basins to shallow intraplate fault rupture, emphasizing the importance of microzonation and earthquake-resistant engineering.
properties.source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (Event ID usp000ekfv)

properties.name: 1992 Flores Earthquake & Tsunami
properties.description: A major Mw 7.8 back-arc subduction thrust earthquake off northern Flores that triggered destructive coastal tsunamis up to 26 meters high.
properties.evidence_description: Teleseismic fault-plane solutions, field tsunami runup elevation measurements (up to 26 m), and coastal damage field logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Seismograms and coastal runup surveys provide physical evidence supporting back-arc thrust faulting and localized tsunami displacement.
properties.geological_explanation: A shallow back-arc thrust fault rupture along the Flores Thrust zone displaced sea floor water, producing catastrophic localized tsunami runup along the Maumere coastline.
properties.why_it_matters: The 1992 Flores event demonstrated that back-arc thrust faulting north of the Sunda Arc can generate localized megathrust-scale earthquakes and severe coastal tsunamis.
properties.source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (Event ID usp0005j81) / Tsuji et al. (1995)

properties.name: 2018 Palu Earthquake, Liquefaction & Tsunami
properties.description: A Mw 7.5 strike-slip earthquake along the Palu-Koro Fault that triggered severe soil liquefaction and bay-confined submarine landslide tsunamis.
properties.evidence_description: InSAR satellite surface deformation maps, flow liquefaction landslide field surveys in Petobo/Balaroa, and Palu Bay tsunami tide logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Satellite radar deformation and field damage surveys provide direct evidence for complex strike-slip liquefaction and bay tsunami interactions.
properties.geological_explanation: Strike-slip faulting caused extreme shaking in saturated alluvial sediments leading to flow liquefaction, while coastal submarine slope failures displaced Palu Bay waters.
properties.why_it_matters: The 2018 Palu event highlighted complex multi-hazard interactions, where strike-slip faulting caused severe urban liquefaction and bay-confined submarine landslide tsunamis.

properties.name: 1815 Tambora Paroxysmal Eruption
properties.description: Explosive VEI-7 super-eruption of Mount Tambora on Sumbawa, releasing 100 cubic km of tephra and causing global climate cooling.
properties.evidence_description: Historical colonial logbooks, atmospheric sulfate ice core records from Greenland/Antarctica, and worldwide 'Year Without a Summer' climate logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Global stratospheric aerosol ice-core signals and historical harvest failure logs provide empirical evidence supporting extreme climate forcing by explosive volcanic sulfur release.
properties.geological_explanation: Paroxysmal explosive eruption ejected high-altitude aerosol clouds into the stratosphere, scattering sunlight globally.
properties.why_it_matters: Tambora 1815 demonstrates the extreme global atmospheric climate impacts of high-index explosive volcanism.

properties.name: 1963 Mount Agung Volcanic Eruption
properties.description: Explosive basaltic-andesite eruption of Mount Agung in Bali, producing devastating pyroclastic flows and secondary rain lahars.
properties.evidence_description: Documented pyroclastic density current deposit mapping along Northern Bali river channels and global stratospheric aerosol optical depth measurements.
properties.evidence_significance: Field mapping of valley-confined pyroclastic flows provides evidence supporting explosive basaltic-andesite eruptions and associated lahars.
properties.geological_explanation: Explosive column collapse generated fast pyroclastic density currents down northern and eastern flanks of Mount Agung.
properties.why_it_matters: Agung 1963 is a landmark event in Indonesian volcanology, highlighting the severity of pyroclastic flows and secondary volcanic lahars.

properties.name: 2005 Nias-Simeulue Megathrust Earthquake
properties.description: Major Mw 8.6 subduction megathrust earthquake along the Sunda Megathrust off Nias and Simeulue islands.
properties.evidence_description: GPS micro-atoll coral uplift measurements (showing up to 3 m coastal tilt) and USGS global broadband seismograms.
properties.evidence_significance: Uplifted coral micro-atoll rings provide direct geodetic evidence supporting contiguous subduction megathrust slip south of the 2004 rupture zone.
properties.geological_explanation: Interplate subduction stress release caused vertical seafloor uplift along Nias and Simeulue micro-atolls.
properties.why_it_matters: Nias 2005 demonstrated contiguous megathrust segment unzipping following major subduction ruptures.
properties.source: Briggs et al. (2006) Science / USGS (Event ID us2005slav)

properties.name: 2010-2021 Mount Sinabung Eruptive Phase
properties.description: Multi-year lava dome collapse and explosive pyroclastic flow phase of Mount Sinabung following 400 years of dormancy.
properties.evidence_description: Time-series satellite thermal imagery, lava dome growth radar surveys, and continuous pyroclastic flow deposit mapping along the Lau Kawawar valley.
properties.evidence_significance: Satellite radar imagery and pyroclastic deposit surveys provide direct evidence for long-duration lava dome collapse volcanism following 400 years of dormancy.
properties.geological_explanation: Persistent dome extrusion and gravitational collapse generated recurring pyroclastic flows down river valleys.
properties.why_it_matters: Sinabung 2010-2021 illustrates long-duration volcano reactivation and multi-year displacement hazards.

properties.name: 2018 Anak Krakatau Flank Collapse & Tsunami
properties.description: Catastrophic southwest flank collapse of Anak Krakatau volcano triggering non-seismic tsunamis across Sunda Strait coastal zones.
properties.evidence_description: Sentinel-1 SAR satellite radar imagery showing 50% volcano volume collapse into the sea, tide gauge tsunami records, and bathymetric sonar surveys.
properties.evidence_significance: Synthetic aperture radar satellite deformation and tide gauge records provide physical evidence supporting submarine landslide tsunamigenesis without antecedent seismic warning.
properties.geological_explanation: Subaerial and submarine slope failure displaced ocean water masses in Sunda Strait.
properties.why_it_matters: Anak Krakatau 2018 demonstrated non-seismic volcanic landslide tsunami hazards in island arc settings.
properties.source: PVMBG / Walter et al. (2019) Nature Communications

properties.name: 2021 Mount Semeru Pyroclastic Density Current & Lahar
properties.description: Dome collapse pyroclastic flow and rain-triggered lahar disaster at Mount Semeru in Lumajang, East Java.
properties.evidence_description: Documented Curah Kobokan river valley block-and-ash flow mapping, rain-triggered secondary lahar deposits, and satellite thermal anomaly logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Valley debris mapping and rainfall gauge records provide evidence supporting heavy rain destabilization of active lava domes generating destructive lahars.
properties.geological_explanation: Heavy monsoonal rainfall eroded active lava dome material at Jonggring Saloko crater, precipitating valley pyroclastic flows and lahars.
properties.why_it_matters: Semeru 2021 highlights how monsoon precipitation interacts with active lava domes to generate rapid multi-hazard volcanic disasters.
